comments.text: Actually, these neighborhoods are all over North Dallas. I lived in a 15 minute city and LOVED it. Luxury apartment. All the bells and whistles that come with luxury apartments. Whole Foods, FedEx, restaurants, a nail salon, CVS pharmacy, a Wells Fargo bank, Starbucks on the corner, all on one city block. On the other end of the apartments was a nice city park with a playground, jogging trails through a creek area, a regional nature preserve next to it, one street light to the biggest north-south freeway in the South… we had a big plaza in the “city square” where we had Saturday morning yoga, picnics, outdoor concerts and movies where people brought blankets and lawn chairs to watch. We had a neighborhood “trolley” to take to around the neighborhood for free if you didn’t want to walk a full mile. The light rail train stopped there- easy access to anywhere in Dallas… the one thing that concerns me about future smart cities is having travel restrictions for outside of the neighborhood. Frisco is one of the most expensive suburbs in Texas. The Dallas Cowboys have a gorgeous practice stadium there. All of the famous luxury brands and international corporations (like Toyota) are there and in Plano. It is super nice there. The people are friendly, everyone has a dog (apparently), the public schools are the best in Texas, just a super place to raise a family. Homes typically start at $1M+. So, I hear you. If you’re from the country, you wouldn’t like it at all. But us city folks in Texas love it. ❤
